lines.en: Another weekend morning is another chance to hang out with Touka.
Or, since Touka doesn’t seem to be around right now, a chance to hang out with her mom and a dejected lesbian.
Weekends are awesome.
: Morning. Where’s everyone else?
: Oh, Sensei. Good day to you. Were you intending to sit in on practice this morning?
: Yeah, I’m sure that’s exactly why he’s here.
: I guess that’s one way to put it. How about you, though? I don’t bump into you over here very often.
: Just how frequently are you trespassing in my kyudojo, Arakawa? You know you’re not supposed to be here.
: I’m sorry, I just missed you so much.
: And I miss sleep, but you don’t see me spending day after day in bed.
: You know, I really wish I did. You need it.
: I was just dropping by to check in on my daughter. But I know she doesn’t like it when I watch her participate in sports, so I wasn’t planning on staying very long.
: Unfortunately, Tsubasa picked the worst day to do this on account of the girls spending today’s morning practice tending to and maintaining their equipment.
: Tsubasa? Since when are you two on a first-name basis? I didn’t even realize you knew each other.
: We didn’t until just moments ago. And I’m the one who proposed we address each other by our first names as I see no reason to be so formal with a fellow alumna of Higashigaoka Girls’ Academy.
: Fellow alumna? But didn’t you go to some super-rich girl school for, like...you know, really rich people? With good manners and all of that stuff?
: I did attend such an academy, yes.
: And...you’re saying Wakana did too?
: Unless I’ve been deceived, that is what I am saying. Yes.
: You’re a private school girl?
: Why do you sound so surprised?
: You know, if anything, I think this actually helps me understand you even better.
: Meanwhile, I’d be shocked to discover you had any sort of formal education whatsoever.
: You two didn’t go to school together, did you?
: Oh, heavens no. I’m much, much older than Wakana. She hasn’t even finished her twenties yet.
: Oh, right. She’s so lifeless that I forget she’s younger than me sometimes.
: This guy...
: How old are you, Tsubasa? I don’t think I’ve asked.
: And for good reason. It’s incredibly impolite to ask a woman her age.
: It’s also incredibly impolite to add several years to it.
: If you don’t mind, Sensei, I’d prefer to keep that information confidential. You don’t see me asking you for your age, do you?
: Don’t need to. I’m 31. Now you know and I get to find out how old you are as well. It's only fair.
: Oh my. No wonder you’re still so full of life. You’re so young. And with Wakana only several years your junior, the two of you would make excellent-
: Enemies.
: ...Enemies, indeed.
: We’re the good kind of enemies, though. The ones who secretly really care about one another deep down.
: The only thing I care about is regaining control of the archery range. Get out of here, Arakawa. Go crawl back into your hole.
: What she really means to say is, “I can’t wait until I see you again.” To which I would agree.
: No, what I really mean to say is “Go crawl back into your hole.” Which is exactly what I said because, unlike you, I can get by without sucking the life force out of everyone around me.
: Are you sure? Because apart from you being out in the sun right now, being a vampire would kind of explain a lot.
: I want you to fucking die.
: Now, now — I understand there’s a bit of hostility between you two, but if you truly do care for one another as you say, you’ll refrain from turning this archery range into a crime scene.
: Sensei, seeing as I’ll be unable to watch my daughter’s practice today, would you care to spend the afternoon with me instead? A nice walk around the grounds seems refreshing, yes?
: Are you sure you want to spend your time with him? Would you not be better off snapping a twig off of a bush and conversing with that instead?
: Of course not. I wouldn’t want to dirty my gloves.
: You know what? I’ll take it. A victory over a twig might not sound like much to most people, but for me it’s a pretty big deal.
: Would you be so obliged as to join us, Wakana? It isn’t very often I bump into alumnae and I’d greatly enjoy the company of someone with a similar background. No offense to Sensei, of course.
: None taken. I wouldn’t have fit in somewhere like that anyway.
: You weren’t even the right sex to be admitted, Arakawa. And no, I’ll respectfully decline your invitation and leave you with your twig. I should be checking on my students anyway.
: Perhaps the next time I drop by, then. It was nice speaking with you, Wakana.
: It was nice speaking with you as well.
: Not you, though.
: We’re friends, I swear.
: Close ones, at that. The way she told you to “crawl back into your hole” was absolutely dripping with positive sentiment.
: Now then, shall we go? I, regretfully, don’t have much time to spare today. And I’d like to make the most of what I do have that I possibly can.
: Does a stroll around the range fit your schedule, Arakawa-Sensei?
: Oh, have I graduated from just “Sensei?” I get to have a two-part name now?
: That didn’t come across as disrespectful, did it?
: Not at all. But I was also just called a twig moments ago and didn’t mind, so titles clearly don’t mean much to me.
: In that case, I suppose I’ll start using your last name more often. We are business partners now, after all.
: We...are?
: Walk with me. There’s something we need to discuss.
: Oh god, what is it now?
: After discussing the Chosokabe matter with my daughter, it appears we’re ready to move forward.
: Okay...and “moving forward” means?
: Waiting for you to trigger the magnetic reaction that will pull Chika closer to safety, of course.
: Touka has agreed to listing several of the additional rooms in your complex at a rate well beneath what they’re actually worth.
: After all, the goal in investing in the property was never to generate income, but moreso to give her an understanding of how the system and property management work as a whole.
: Is...generating revenue not a part of the “system and property management?”
: It is. Of course it is. But this is closer to a small project for her than something she’s meant to live off of. Everything she needs and wants is already supplied by the Tsukioka Foundation.
: Wouldn’t it make more sense to...let Chika keep her old apartment and just toss her the key to a new one in the event she changes her mind and wants to move?
: That’s essentially what we’re doing, Arakawa-Sensei. Just instead of tossing her the key, we’re leaving it on the ground for her to pick up.
: Unless you don’t want her closer to you for some reason. And that’s certainly not the case, is it?
: I mean...it could definitely cause some problems.
: Ohh?
: You weren’t intending to use my daughter’s generous gift as a secret love nest, were you? Does having your girlfriend in the same building throw a wrench into things?
: It’s a little more complicated than that. I’ve barely even spent any time in that apartment...
: But it feels weird to just uproot someone’s life under the guise of “this is better for them” when that shouldn’t be our choice to make.
: A well-thought out answer and impressive deflection away from my “love nest” accusation. Though, I wouldn’t say it’s one I agree with.
: And why’s that?
: Isn’t it obvious?
: Most people aren’t smart enough to make their own decisions.
: The world would crash and burn if it weren’t for those of us who can bend it to our will...and shape it back into its proper form.
: Chika’s an amazing girl and I care for her and empathize with her — but she isn’t smart.
: She is though. You don’t know her like I do.
: I know that she has a sexual relationship with an adult male. And that she’s turning down free aid that would make both her and her sister’s lives easier.
: The first of which can be justified under the pretense of you providing some sort of benefit — emotional, physical or financial — but the second?
: The second is pure negligence and stubbornness and will only force her down the same road her mother had to walk before her.
: If I need to reshape things one more time to prevent her from enduring such tragedy, so be it. I do it out of the kindness of my heart and ask for nothing in return.
: But doing things your way just seems like it’s providing an illusion of free will. It’s not giving Chika or...anyone else you deem “not smart enough” the chance to burn out or fail on their own.
: Sometimes, people need that if they’re going to improve.
: I agree. But this isn’t a score on a test or a poorly-made resume- it is a life. Two lives, even.
: What’s wrong with playing God when the one we dreamt up never wants to come outside?
: As long as nothing crashes and burns, we’ll have succeeded. So you can keep playing the “good cop” all you want while believing the girls you know so well are capable of making their own decisions-
: Or you can leave it to the “bad cop” who just-so-happens to have good intentions.
: You really are “manipulative in the good way,” aren’t you?
: I really am.
: I respect your speech and all. It’s nice hearing from someone with a mindset like that. But it’s making me a little confused about your stance on Touka.
: How so?
: Do you not think her life is at stake by throwing her into my class at such an impressionable part of her life?

: She might have a healthy, albeit extremely obnoxious, little sister...but this is her education we’re talking about and you’ve figured out by now that’s, like...the last thing on my list of priorities.
: I guess what I’m asking is...why is she allowed to make her own decisions, but Chika can’t? Is it really just the sister thing that changes all of this?
: Not at all. In fact, my repeated presence at this school should be the only hint you need in regard to her autonomy.
: There are several mistakes I want her to make- and she is well on her way to making them.
: But it all circles back around to what I want for her as I would never put her into a position where that outcome would be unachievable.
: You really are just a well-endowed puppeteer, aren’t you?
: Perhaps I am!
: Does that make you my puppet?
: I guess that depends on whether or not you think I’m “smart enough” to make my own decisions.
: Surely you’re not making me out to be some sort of villain, are you, Arakawa-Sensei?
: I’m sure a man of your position can understand my point of view, no?
: I possess both the intellect and influence to make anything I want a reality. Why would I not do that?
: Again, you’ve got a point. I’d probably do the same thing in your position.
: Which is why I like you. But that’s enough about me and my points of view — why don’t you tell me a little about yourself?
: What do you believe in?
: What’s your favorite food?
: What kind of music do you like?
: I have so many questions for you.
: This might come as a surprise given my outstanding charisma and boisterous attitude, but I don’t really like talking about myself.
: But you’ve learned so much about me so far. And you’ve been addressing me as “Tsubasa” this whole time. Do you not want to be my friend after all?
: That’s not it. I’m just not that exciting. That’s really all it is.
: Ohh?
: Perhaps I’ll look into you on my own, then? I can’t have my daughters, biological or not, spending so much time around a man with a shady background, can I?
: You’re not trying to intimidate me right now, are you? Because the smirk and the fact that I have to look up at you were more than enough to do that without the vague threat.
: That’s not what I want.
: I’ve spent so much time looking down on others that being up here is just more comfortable for me. That’s all.
: You’re an interesting person, Arakawa-Sensei. And I really do want to learn more about you as I assume you’ll be growing quite familiar with my family in the years to come.
: That “quite familiar” emphasis was a little suggestive, don’t you think?
: You’ll have to forgive me if my...sincerest thoughts managed to leak out. I just meant that I don’t intend to let you walk away from us is all.
: We’ve all taken quite the interest in you.
: But, with you unwilling to tell me any more about yourself, it appears that I’ll have to look further into you on my own after all.
: Come now. You can escort me to the car.
Tsubasa gestures as if she’s pulling on puppet strings, but I follow her up the stairs out of my own free will.
Or...what I think is my own free will but is actually just her masterminding my every move like she was alluding to earlier.
She reminds me of someone else in a way.
But the two of them are completely different.
I can understand what Tsubasa wants...and it really does seem like she just wants this world to be a better place.
But “better” is subjective...and she likely hasn’t failed enough in life to know that what “she” wants isn’t what’s best for everyone.
Is she like me — so self-centered that she’ll never be able to look past that?
Can she keep believing what she’s done is right even when it’s wrong in every other sense of the word?
Or is she someone who can change the way she thinks...and reshape herself along with the world she treats as a globe, spinning infinitely beneath her finger?
I don’t know.
I’m not close enough to her yet.
But...
I don’t mind having her yank my strings a little longer if it changes that.
Tsubasa’s affection has increased to [tsubasa_love]!
